title: First day at Datacore
subtitle: Onboarding: what ML really is, the project lifecycle and team roles

seo.title: Machine learning vs rules: when you don't need a model
seo.h1: Half the “ML tasks” you are handed are solved by an if-else
seo.lead: Four requests from a product manager. We decide which of them genuinely need a model and which are closed by a twenty-line rule — the rule wins more often than people expect.
seo.description: When a task needs machine learning and when rules are enough: the ML project lifecycle, the roles on a team and an honest test for choosing between them.

title: First task: exploratory data analysis
subtitle: Python, Pandas and EDA: the team lead wants a sales data report by Friday

seo.title: Exploratory data analysis: EDA on a real dataset
seo.h1: Revenue grew, profit did not. We found out why without a model
seo.lead: EDA is not “looking at the data”, it is an investigation. One report over 50,000 orders turns up duplicates, missing values and the real cause of the margin collapse.
seo.description: What EDA is and how to find why profit is falling: duplicates on the business key, missing values, outliers and distributions in pandas over 50,000 orders.

title: Marketing argues: did the discount help?
subtitle: Statistics and visualization: distributions, hypotheses and an A/B test of a promo

seo.title: A/B testing and p-value explained on a real case
seo.h1: The discount lifted conversion — and brought in less money
seo.lead: Conversion moved from 5.8% to 6.4%. We work out whether that is a win or noise, and why the answer the business actually needs sits in revenue rather than in the p-value.
seo.description: How to check whether an A/B result is significant: hypotheses, p-value, confidence intervals and sample size — and why the winning group lost on money.

title: Predicting delivery cost
subtitle: Linear regression: your first model, gradient descent and coefficient interpretation

seo.title: Linear regression in practice: MAE, RMSE, coefficients
seo.h1: The first model saved millions — and it was a linear regression
seo.lead: Predicting delivery cost instead of charging a city average. A simple model you can explain to finance coefficient by coefficient, and it beats the baseline threefold.
seo.description: The first working model: linear regression, gradient descent, MAE against RMSE and how to explain coefficients to the business instead of a black box.

title: Customers are leaving: a churn model
subtitle: Logistic regression and classification: predicting churn before the customer is gone

seo.title: Customer churn model: probabilities, not labels
seo.h1: The insight turned out to be worth more than the model
seo.lead: Retention cannot call 200,000 people, it needs a ranked list. That is where the real requirement comes from: not a “will churn” label but a probability.
seo.description: Predicting customer churn: logistic regression, the sigmoid and the threshold, why the business needs probabilities and how coefficients turn into decisions.

title: A 99%-accurate model that doesn't work
subtitle: Quality metrics: precision, recall, ROC-AUC and the cost of errors in anti-fraud

seo.title: Precision, recall, ROC-AUC: why 99% accuracy fails
seo.h1: 99.2% accurate — and it caught zero fraudsters
seo.lead: Fraud is 0.8% of the data. A model that always answers “not fraud” scores 99.2% and catches nobody. We look at what to measure instead of accuracy.
seo.description: Walked through an anti-fraud case: the confusion matrix, precision against recall, ROC-AUC against PR-AUC and why the threshold comes from the cost of errors.

title: Credit scoring: data decides everything
subtitle: Feature engineering: aggregates, categorical encoding, handling missing values

seo.title: Feature engineering: encoding, gaps and leakage
seo.h1: A weak model on strong features beats a strong model on weak ones
seo.lead: Building a feature matrix for credit scoring out of three tables, and stepping around the trap that makes a model look brilliant on history and collapse in production.
seo.description: How features are built: aggregates over time windows, category encoding, missing values and the trap of a feature from the future that breaks a model in production.

title: Churn v2: boosting vs the forest
subtitle: Decision trees, Random Forest and gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost)

seo.title: Gradient boosting vs random forest on tabular data
seo.h1: On tabular data, boosting beats neural networks
seo.lead: Logistic regression scored 0.834, the random forest 0.861, boosting 0.874. We work out where the gap comes from and why trees keep winning on tables.
seo.description: Trees, bagging and boosting: how a random forest differs from gradient boosting, which hyperparameters matter and why they beat neural networks on tables.

title: Incident: the model fell apart in production
subtitle: Validation, overfitting and data leakage — a real failure post-mortem

seo.title: Data leakage and overfitting: a production post-mortem
seo.h1: 0.97 on the test set, 0.61 in production
seo.lead: We investigate someone else's incident: a random split of time-ordered data, a scaler fitted before the split, and a feature that does not exist at decision time.
seo.description: Five kinds of data leakage, honest validation schemes over time and groups, and why a metric that looks too good is a warning rather than a result.

title: Squeezing out 2% more quality
subtitle: Hyperparameter tuning: grid search, random search and Optuna

seo.title: Hyperparameter tuning: grid, random search and Optuna
seo.h1: A gain of 0.005 against a spread of 0.004 is noise
seo.lead: One day and one server shared by three teams. We tune deliberately and learn to tell a real improvement from a random swing of cross-validation.
seo.description: How to tune a model in a day: why random search beats a grid, what Optuna does and how to tell a real gain apart from cross-validation noise.

title: Fraud: 1 fraudster per 1000 honest users
subtitle: Imbalanced classes: class weights, sampling, threshold selection

seo.title: Imbalanced classes: weights, sampling and thresholds
seo.h1: 93% of the alerts are false — and the economics still work
seo.lead: One fraudster per thousand honest users, 500 manual checks a day and two errors with very different price tags. The threshold here is arithmetic, not 0.5 by default.
seo.description: A 1:1000 imbalance: class weights against SMOTE, why PR-AUC is more honest than ROC-AUC and how to derive a threshold in money rather than in metrics.

title: Who are our customers, really?
subtitle: Clustering and unsupervised learning: customer base segmentation

seo.title: Customer segmentation: K-Means, RFM and choosing k
seo.h1: A cluster without a name is not a result
seo.lead: There are no labels here and no correct answer. Segmentation quality is measured by whether marketing can do something different with each segment tomorrow.
seo.description: Segmenting a customer base without labels: RFM features, K-Means, the elbow method and silhouette — and why the real quality test here is a business one.

title: "Frequently bought together": recommendations
subtitle: Recommender systems: collaborative filtering and ranking metrics

seo.title: Recommender systems: collaborative filtering and NDCG
seo.h1: The model learned that phones go with cases, knowing nothing about products
seo.lead: Matrix factorisation splits purchase history into tastes and properties. Product affinity falls out of the numbers, not out of the descriptions.
seo.description: How recommendations work: matrix factorisation and embeddings, the cold start problem and the ranking metrics precision@k, recall@k and NDCG.

title: The warehouse is overstocked: demand forecasting
subtitle: Time series: trend, seasonality, lag features and honest validation

seo.title: Demand forecasting: time series, lags and validation
seo.h1: A naive forecast gets you 80% of the way to a complex model
seo.lead: In time series the order of the data is information, and the usual cross-validation quietly lies. We start from baselines that are harder to beat than they look.
seo.description: Forecasting demand for 2000 products: trend and seasonality, lag features, rolling validation and why MAPE is a poor metric choice in retail.

title: Support is drowning in tickets
subtitle: NLP: from TF-IDF to transformers — automatic ticket classification

seo.title: Text classification: TF-IDF against transformers
seo.h1: The bigger model is more accurate — and does not pay for itself
seo.lead: Five thousand tickets a day and 55 person-hours spent purely on sorting them. We choose between three options on F1 together with latency and hardware.
seo.description: Auto-classifying support tickets: TF-IDF with a linear model against a fine-tuned transformer, macro-F1, latency and the confidence threshold.

title: Meet neural networks
subtitle: Deep learning: the neuron, layers, backpropagation and your first PyTorch net

seo.title: Neural networks: backpropagation and overfitting
seo.h1: If you have never overfitted a network, you cannot train one
seo.lead: The network without any magic: neuron, layers, backpropagation. Then we overfit it on purpose to see exactly what that looks like on the training curves.
seo.description: How a neural network works: neurons, layers, activation functions and backpropagation, training in PyTorch and a deliberate overfitting experiment.

title: Defects on the conveyor: computer vision
subtitle: CV: convolutional networks, transfer learning and quality control in manufacturing

seo.title: Computer vision: CNNs and transfer learning
seo.h1: Four thousand photos. Training from scratch will not fly
seo.lead: Defect detection on a packing line: why convolution saves millions of weights, and how to fine-tune a pretrained network instead of starting from zero.
seo.description: Quality control from photos: how convolution works, why transfer learning is needed on a small dataset and how to set the threshold by the cost of a defect.

title: The interview in reverse: ML System Design
subtitle: Designing an ML system end-to-end: from business metric to architecture

seo.title: ML system design: how to answer at the interview
seo.h1: What separates a mid-level engineer is designing the whole system
seo.lead: A one-sentence brief, exactly as it arrives at an interview. We unpack it with a framework: from the business metric to architecture, constraints and risks.
seo.description: The ML system design framework: from business metric to a retrieval and ranking architecture, the latency budget, guardrail metrics and the rollout plan.

title: The model is ready. Now — to production
subtitle: MLOps: an API service, Docker, monitoring, data drift and retraining

seo.title: MLOps: shipping a model, monitoring and data drift
seo.h1: A model without monitoring is an incident that has not happened yet
seo.lead: A model somebody runs by hand on Mondays is not a product. We turn it into a service with an API, versions, drift monitoring and a rollback plan.
seo.description: How a model becomes a service: FastAPI and Docker, versioning, three layers of monitoring, PSI for drift and the shadow, canary and rollback sequence.

title: Finale: defending your project before the CTO
subtitle: Capstone project + final exam: you are ready for a Middle ML Engineer position

seo.title: End-to-end ML project: the mid-level engineer exam
seo.h1: Business problem first, then the data, and only then the model
seo.lead: The final project end to end: from framing to an operations plan, defended in front of the CTO and the product manager. Everything before it converges here.
seo.description: The capstone project: framing, leak-free features, validation, a threshold from the cost matrix, an A/B test with guardrails and an operations plan.

title: Advanced · Before writing code: the Design Doc
subtitle: From the “ML System Design” book: problem space, cost of a mistake, design doc structure and review

seo.title: The ML design doc: problem space and cost of error
seo.h1: The best project is the one you decided not to build
seo.lead: A month before the first line of code. We write the design doc: where it hurts, what that costs, what we will not do and on what condition the project is closed.
seo.description: What goes into a design doc before any code: problem space, the cost of error both ways, anti-goals and a stopping criterion. Based on the Manning book.

title: Advanced · Metrics, data, validation, baselines
subtitle: Hierarchy of metrics, sample-wise learning curve, adversarial validation and the baseline ladder

seo.title: Metric hierarchy, baselines and adversarial validation
seo.h1: Half an hour spent reading errors beats a week of tuning
seo.lead: Loss, offline metric, online metric and money are four different things. We stack them into a pyramid and build the ladder of baselines from the bottom up.
seo.description: The early stage of a project: a metric pyramid from loss to money, the baseline ladder, adversarial validation and error analysis instead of blind tuning.

title: Advanced · Integration, A/B, monitoring, ownership
subtitle: Training vs inference pipelines, debrief, drift types, fallback hierarchy and bus factor

seo.title: A/B testing ML systems, drift types and ownership
seo.h1: Who fixes the model at three in the morning
seo.lead: The model beat every baseline, so the easy part is over. Next come pipelines, an honest experiment, monitoring and the question of who is accountable for it.
seo.description: What turns a model into a system: training and inference pipelines, A/B design, drift types, the fallback hierarchy and accountability inside the team.
